topic: Control physics and hardware evolution of jyjblrd/single-propeller-drone
method: Read-only research using both available web search systems, primary papers, university publications, author posts and repository/CAD reads. No flight or bench experiments performed.

sources.title: I Built a Drone With Only One Motor – And a Poor Man's High Speed Camera
sources.relevance: First-person report of PPA-CF hinged hub, complementary lag/pitch response, approximately 300 torque pulses per second, near-20,000 RPM, motor-local pulse generation, slowly rotating body and once-per-body-revolution infrared heading correction.
sources.limits: Author statements, not independent measurements or peer review. Exact posting day was not reliably exposed in inspected page. Duplicate posts are not independent corroboration. Linked video could not be retrieved and was not watched.

sources.title: single-propeller-drone: Under-actuated drone with only one motor
sources.relevance: Authoritative scope of supplied mechanical CAD, media and linked flight/motor-controller forks. STEP product metadata distinguishes earlier blade components from later rocking-blade assembly.
sources.limits: Current root and README inventory is not a complete reconstruction specification. No published BOM, validated energy/fatigue dataset or complete calibration/assembly instructions in inspected main repository. STEP default material labels must not be interpreted as manufacturing requirements.

sources.title: Underactuated Rotor for Simple Micro Air Vehicles
sources.relevance: Explains inclined hinge lead-lag/pitch coupling and rotor-synchronous sinusoidal torque amplitude/phase. Provides canonical bibliography for 2013, 2015 and 2018 work.
sources.limits: Project overview spans multiple vehicle configurations. Two-rotor/full-actuation capabilities are not properties of a one-motor aircraft.

sources.title: An Underactuated Propeller for Attitude Control in Micro Air Vehicles
sources.relevance: Original direct torque-modulated, passively hinged rotor concept and two-motor coaxial flight demonstration; clarifies mean torque versus cyclic torque roles.
sources.limits: Flight platform has two motors. No direct validation of Bird's rotor geometry, print process or near-20,000-RPM regime.

sources.title: Flight Performance of a Swashplateless Micro Air Vehicle
sources.relevance: Integrated encoder-based cyclic control, 227 g coaxial aircraft with 30 cm main rotor, hover loading/power experiments and motion-capture trajectory tracking.
sources.limits: Two propellers/two motors and external tracking. Its mass, performance and trim-power results cannot be assigned to Bird's aircraft.

sources.title: Cyclic Blade Pitch Control Without a Swashplate for Small Helicopters
sources.venue: Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics 41(3), pages 689–700
sources.relevance: Detailed lag/flap model with variable hub speed; compares measured torque, speed, lag/pitch and flap first harmonics. Shows stiction threshold, amplitude-dependent phase accuracy and significant flap-amplitude prediction error. Direct experimental-design precedent.
sources.limits: Model and tests describe the authors' articulated rotor near hover. Actual mechanism, materials, friction and aerodynamic conditions must be identified again. Author manuscript copyright year 2017 differs from final 2018 journal issue.

sources.title: Scalability of Cyclic Control without Blade Pitch Actuators
sources.venue: AIAA SciTech / Atmospheric Flight Mechanics Conference 2018
sources.relevance: Dynamically similar 10 cm/1 m rotor experiments, reported 300–9,000 RPM envelope, effects of nonuniform mass/inertia, motor/drive identification with known added inertias, and implications of larger/slower rotors for modulation demand.
sources.limits: Similarity assumptions and bench experiments are not qualification of a 20,000-RPM printed rotor. Scale trends must preserve relevant dimensionless mechanical/aerodynamic parameters.

sources.title: Emulating a Fully Actuated Aerial Vehicle using Two Actuators
sources.relevance: Two articulated rotors independently vector thrust to separate translation/orientation. Helps prevent conflation of single-motor cyclic capability with full six-degree-of-freedom actuation.
sources.limits: Two-actuator coaxial platform. Independent yaw and force/moment capabilities do not transfer intact to one actuator.

sources.title: A self-rotating, single-actuated UAV with extended sensor field of view for autonomous navigation
sources.relevance: PULSAR: one-motor rotor-synchronous control, naturally rotating body, onboard LiDAR navigation and complete-system power benchmark. Reported 26.7% hover-power reduction against specified quadrotor with similar total disk area and same avionics payload.
sources.limits: Different complete aircraft and operating conditions. Power reduction is benchmark-specific, not a motor-count law or predicted saving for Bird. Navigation payload/performance must not be silently transferred.

sources.title: An autonomous single-actuator UAV with omnidirectional field of view, high agility, and collision resistance
sources.relevance: PULSAR II: data-driven nonlinear propulsion identification/compensation; S² MPC; differential-flatness planning; solid protective frame; fictional-frame disturbance observer decoupling self-rotation; μ-synthesis robustness tuning.
sources.limits: Full Nature text redirected to unavailable authentication and PMC returned browser verification. University abstract and indexed publisher text were read; no claim of full methods/supplement inspection. Paper-linked GitHub repository returned 404; no code was inspected. No PULSAR II numerical performance is attributed to Bird.

sources.title: Adaptive Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion for Attitude Control of Micro Air Vehicles
authors: Guido C. H. E. de Croon
sources.venue: Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics 39(3), pages 450–461
sources.relevance: INDI uses angular-acceleration estimates and control effectiveness; explicitly addresses measurement/actuator delay, changing effectiveness and propeller momentum. Motivates a carefully filtered, identified inner-loop comparison.
sources.limits: University abstract/record read; linked full manuscript retrieval failed. Not an implementation or validation for a passively hinged single-rotor plant. Sensor vibration, averaging and waveform-effectiveness mapping require new experiments.

sources.title: Autonomous Quadrotor Flight despite Rotor Failure with Onboard Vision Sensors: Frames vs. Events
sources.venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 6(2), pages 580–587
sources.relevance: Real-world onboard-estimated position control during complete loss of one quadrotor rotor, with high yaw rotation; useful reduced-attitude and estimator analogy, and limits of frame cameras during rotation.
sources.limits: Three functioning rotors remain. Does not prove one-actuator controllability, Bird's margins, or survival of sole-motor failure. Published article DOI has 2020 registration; journal year is 2021.

sources.title: Cyclic speed modulation for swashplateless mechanism in micro unmanned helicopter control
sources.venue: Aerospace Science and Technology 176, Part A, article 112010
sources.relevance: Current primary study explicitly investigates closed-loop FOC cyclic-speed modulation and limitations of tracking under high-speed conditions, directly relevant to the motor-bandwidth research question.
sources.limits: Publisher indexed abstract/highlights read; direct full page blocked and paid PDF not inspected. No numerical improvement, operating RPM, stability guarantee or replication is claimed. September is issue date, not asserted exact online-first date.

sources.title: UIUC Propeller Database — Volume 2
sources.relevance: Static RPM sweeps and wind-tunnel thrust/torque coefficient data, measured geometry, printed-propeller configurations, and power coefficients derived from measured torque/speed. Reference discipline for energy and aerodynamic benchmarking.
sources.limits: Dataset specimens are not Bird's articulated rotor or finned-wake installation. Performance must not be extrapolated outside measured geometry/RPM/Reynolds conditions without validation.

sources.title: PPA-CF — manufacturer material information
sources.relevance: Explicit dependence of printed properties on orientation, walls, infill, geometry and dry/wet conditioning; supports treating the manufacturing process as an experimental variable.
sources.limits: Indexed official manufacturer text read; direct storefront returned 402. Marketing/static specimen properties do not establish fatigue life, allowable rotor speed or strength of the author's actual printed parts. No supplier purchase or cost recommendation.
